seats: a secular academic scholar of the Bible

fixes.row: Given, taken away, thrown out, restored: ... "a kingdom of priests"
fixes.why: Two of this row's four examples (Exod 19:6, Rev 5:10) do not show its label: "a kingdom of priests" is neither given, taken away, thrown out nor restored. Putting Sinai's "kingdom of priests" in the same row as Matt 21:43 and Acts 1:6, with the NT verses shown first, files an OT verse under an NT-framed story of transfer and reads a later doctrine back into Exod 19:6. It also cuts apart a thread that belongs together (Exod 19:6, Rev 1:6, Rev 5:10).
fixes.fix: Split. Row A "Given, taken away, thrown out, restored": the OT verses first (1 Sam 15:28, 1 Kgs 11:11, 11:31, 14:8, Dan 5:28), then Matt 8:11-12, 21:43, Luke 13:28-29, 22:30, Acts 1:3, 1:6; examples led by an OT and an NT verse. Row B "A kingdom of priests" (Exod 19:6, Rev 1:6, Rev 5:10), Exod 19:6 first, with the Church-or-Israel note kept for Rev 1:6 and 5:10. That adds a row; offset it by merging row "The keys of the kingdom" into "Enter the kingdom" (see merge fix) if the count matters.

fixes.why: The note opens its first claim with how Israel's kingdom stands to the kingdom of God, a question the Samuel-Kings-Chronicles verses do not ask. It brings the NT question into a row that should be heard on its own terms first.
fixes.fix: Reorder the note: "The human kingdom of Israel and of Judah, as the books of Samuel, Kings and Chronicles tell it." Drop the sentence about Christian traditions here (it is already in the "Given, taken away" row and the David row).

fixes.why: Rev 11:15 ("has become the kingdom of our Lord") and Rev 12:10 ("Now have come ... the kingdom of our God") are the same kind of heavenly announcement, yet 11:15 is filed under "still ahead" and 12:10 under "near or here". That placement leans toward a reading the text does not settle. Luke 19:11 states what the people thought (that it would appear imminently), so it stands under "ahead" while saying "imminent"; the note admits it is not a statement of when.
fixes.fix: Put Rev 11:15 in both rows 12 and 13, or in neither with a note that the Greek is a completed verb inside a vision of the end; state that Rev 11:15 and 12:10 are the same sort of announcement. Take Luke 19:11 out of "still ahead" and leave it in the parable/reign row.

fixes.row: Said as near, or as here
fixes.why: Matt 11:12 ("has been forcefully advancing") and Luke 16:16 ("is being preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it") are among the most disputed verses of the whole word and are filed, bare, under "here". The note covers Luke 17:21, Rev 1:9 and Heb 12:28 but not these. Luke 21:31 is a "near" said of a future event, which the note passes over.
fixes.fix: Add to the note: "Matt 11:12 and Luke 16:16 are among the hardest verses of the word; the Greek verbs can be read as the kingdom advancing or as being pressed, and the page does not choose. Luke 21:31 says 'near' of the events that Jesus has just described."

fixes.row: Said as still ahead / The kingdom of God (waiting)
fixes.why: Joseph "was waiting for the kingdom of God" (Mark 15:43, Luke 23:51; the Greek is prosdechomenos) is as plainly forward-looking as anything in the ahead row, yet it sits only under "The kingdom of God". The ahead row therefore under-counts the text's expectation, and the arc from a waiting Israel to Joseph at the cross is lost.
fixes.fix: Add Mark 15:43 and Luke 23:51 to "Said as still ahead"; they say what a person was looking for, with no claim about when.

fixes.why: The note says Matt 6:33 stands elsewhere "where the verse's own words are not 'kingdom of God' as one phrase". The Berean prints "seek first the kingdom of God", so a reader sees the contradiction at once; if the hub's Greek lacks "of God" there, the note must say that, and say so as a finding.
fixes.fix: Rewrite: "Matt 6:33 is in the row of the kingdom sought; the Berean prints 'of God' there and the rule that builds this row did not find it with the Greek word beside it. Eph 5:5 reads 'of Christ and of God'." Or add Matt 6:33 to this row as well. Mark the finding in the verse if the original reads otherwise.

fixes.row: The LORD’s kingdom, and the LORD over every kingdom
fixes.why: Ps 45 is a royal wedding psalm addressed to a human king; the Hebrew words stand beside a king and a queen. Filing Ps 45:6 under the LORD's kingdom while Heb 1:8 sits in "Of the Son" places the psalm by a later reading, even with a note, and the row order makes the note a footnote to a decision already made.
fixes.fix: Put Ps 45:6 in the row of Israel's and Judah's own kingdom (the king the psalm addresses) and keep it also here, so both placements show; add a sentence to the Son row's note for Heb 1:8: "quotes Ps 45:6; readers part on whom the psalm addresses and the page does not choose".

fixes.why: The note names only pre-, post- and amillennial readings and "Christ's first coming", all Christian schemes, and applies the millennial words to a book that has no thousand years. It omits the Jewish reading and the historical reading that sets Dan 7 against the second-century BC; a scholar would find the list partial and anachronistic.
fixes.fix: Replace the second half of the note: "Readings part on which kingdoms the four are (Babylon, Media, Persia and Greece on one reading; Babylon, Persia, Greece and Rome on another), on when the kingdom 'that will never be destroyed' is set up, and on who 'the saints of the Most High' are. Jewish, historical and Christian readings differ; the page takes no side." Keep the pointer to Rev 20.

fixes.why: These four do not say "theirs is the kingdom": Matt 18:4 is "the greatest in the kingdom", and 18:3, Mark 10:15 and Luke 18:17 are conditions of entering or receiving it. The label promises a possession and the verses give a requirement. All four already sit in the Enter and Receive rows.
fixes.fix: Take Matt 18:3, 18:4, Mark 10:15 and Luke 18:17 out of this row, leaving Matt 5:3, 5:10, Luke 6:20, Matt 19:14, Mark 10:14, Luke 18:16 and Jas 2:5 ("belongs to such as these" fits). Or relabel: "Theirs is the kingdom, and the child as the pattern".

fixes.row: One king’s kingdom, realm or sovereignty
fixes.why: The note says "the Berean's English, the same Hebrew and Aramaic words", which equates h4467 (Hebrew) with h4437 (Aramaic) and the Greek verse; and the last row's note does the same in "The same Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek words". Rev 17:18 is a city that "rules over the kings" (the Greek has basileia, "kingship"), which the label "One king's kingdom" does not show.
fixes.fix: In both notes, say "words that elsewhere in the hub are printed 'kingdom'; each example shows its own word". Move Rev 17:18 out of this row into the royal sense row or the kings-of-the-earth row; Rev 17:12 and 17:17 stay.

fixes.why: Heb 1:8 is a quotation of Ps 45:6 and the note for this row does not say so, though the LORD row's note does. A reader of this row alone meets a bare "Your throne, O God" filed as the Son's.
fixes.fix: Add: "Heb 1:8 quotes Ps 45:6 (also in the rows of the LORD's kingdom and Israel's kingdom); the verse itself says 'about the Son He says'."

fixes.row: The keys of the kingdom, and the kingdom shut
fixes.why: Row count is 27 against 15-25. Matt 23:13 says the kingdom is shut and the leaders neither enter nor let others in, which is the Enter thread. Two verses as a row cuts the keys from the entering they unlock.
fixes.fix: Optional. If the count must fall, merge into "Enter the kingdom" with Matt 16:19's note kept verbatim. If the other seats (Catholic, Orthodox) want Matt 16:19 visible alone, keep it and instead merge "Prayed for, and sought first" into "Said as near" is NOT advised; leave as is and accept 27 with the 66-verse royal-sense row accounting for two.

worker_points.point: 1. Rows 12 and 13: the kingdom now, still to come, or both
worker_points.why: Rev 1:9, Heb 12:28, Col 1:13 and Rev 12:10 are fairly placed with a note naming their tense. The tilts are Rev 11:15 (in ahead, but 12:10 in here), Luke 19:11 (people's view, not text's claim), and the unflagged Matt 11:12 and Luke 16:16. Luke 21:31 is placed by its word "near", which is fine. Waiting (Mark 15:43, Luke 23:51) is absent from ahead.

worker_points.point: 2. Rows 7 and 8: kingdom of heaven and kingdom of God
worker_points.why: "In Matthew alone" is a fact, checked against the 31 verses, not a lean; the note sets Matt 19:23-24 and the parallels side by side and says the page does not call them one. Only the Matt 6:33 sentence needs correcting.

worker_points.point: 3. Row 24: the thousand years, and Luke 19:12-27 in the same row
worker_points.why: The row is built on the verb and the note says the page does not say whom the nobleman stands for; the parable's reign vocabulary is in the text. A reader could take 1 Cor 4:8 (Paul's irony toward the Corinthians) as a sign of the saints' reign, so the note should say it is said to the Corinthians; it already does.
Dan 2:44 and 7:14 in both rows is right. The Daniel note's list of readings is Christian-only and borrows millennial terms; see the Daniel fix.

worker_points.point: 5. Row 21: Israel's kingdom and the kingdom of God
worker_points.why: One row for "taken away", "restored" and "a kingdom of priests" does read as one story, and two of four examples do not show the label. Split as in the first fix.

OT verses first in the verse list; 1 Chr 28:7's condition is named; the note names the Jewish and Christian readings without a verdict. Two of four examples are NT (Luke 1:33, Mark 11:10); acceptable because the row is the promise's repeats, but the examples could be 2 Sam 7:16, 1 Chr 17:14, Isa 9:7, Luke 1:33 to hear the OT first.

worker_points.point: 7. Rows 18, 19: enter, inherit, will not inherit
worker_points.why: The vice lists sit beside "inherit" with the explicit note that traditions part; the John 3:5 readings are listed evenly. The label "how hard" refers to the camel and Acts 14:22 and does not lean. Enter and Receive overlap on Mark 10:15 and Luke 18:17, which is the text's own doubling.
Two verses, a note on whom the keys go to; no verdict. Merge is optional.
Matt 22:2, Luke 14:15 and 13:29 are banquets that say the word; Last Supper verses are named without a reading of the Supper.

worker_points.point: 10. Rows 9, 10 and the catch-all: divine persons by hand
worker_points.why: Heb 1:8 needs the Ps 45 pointer in the Son row; Ps 45:6 should also stand in the Israel/king row (see fix). The catch-all treatment of 2 Tim 4:18 is right.
It stands beside Luke 17:20-21 and Pauline negations, with a note that traditions part; the row order places it after both near and ahead rows, so it does not settle the matter.
Esth 5:3, Mark 6:23 and Luke 4:5-6 are placed as what a king offers and what the devil shows, with no gloss. Rev 17:18 aside (see the different-words fix).

missing.what: Waiting for the kingdom: Joseph of Arimathea, and "not far from the kingdom"; the expectation of a person, not a claim about when
The secret of the kingdom, given to some and withheld from others (the one saying reported in all three synoptic Gospels, the reason for parables)
Sons of the kingdom: those who belong to it, named in the weeds parable and in Matt 8:12

examples_checked: 26 of 27 rows' examples show their label (all four read in the Berean for each row; the exception is the Given/taken away/restored row, where Exod 19:6 and Rev 5:10 are shown for the label "given, taken away, thrown out, restored" and do not show it; Rev 17:18 in row 2 and Matt 18:3-4 in the Theirs row are non-example misfits in the verse lists)
summary: The hub is faithful to the text, keeps the near/ahead/both disputes on neutral ground, keeps the divine persons by hand and sets the OT rows first, but it needs a few repairs. The kingdom-of-priests material is cut away from Sinai and bound to the transfer story, Rev 11:15 and 12:10 are filed on opposite sides of the same question, Ps 45:6 is placed by a later reading, and the Daniel note offers only Christian schemes.
